key_insight: Combining clinical, tumor gene-expression, and circulating tumor DNA data modestly improved machine-learning prediction of progression-free survival in HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer.
clinical_relevance: The findings may support prognostic research and biological hypothesis generation, but do not establish treatment-selection utility or identify new drugs.
method: Integrated baseline data from phase III MONALEESA-2, -3, and -7 trials.
Trained early- and late-fusion models using clinical features, tumor gene expression, and plasma ctDNA.
Evaluated progression-free survival prediction and model-based risk groups in a held-out test set.
evidence_signal: Models were trained on 1,355 patients and tested on 382; late fusion achieved a C-index of 0.727 (95% CI, 0.641–0.799), with low- versus high-risk groups showing a PFS hazard ratio of 0.28 (95% CI, 0.20–0.38).
watch_item: External validation and prospective assessment of clinical utility are needed before implementation beyond the MONALEESA trial populations.
paper_title: Multimodal Machine Learning-Based Clinical and Genomic Prognostic Factors for Progression-Free Survival in Metastatic Breast Cancer Using Phase III MONALEESA Trials
